Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

CleanLASA (development version)

Missing values

  • keep_user_na = TRUE now keeps a missing-value code with its own label, declared SPSS user-missing, for every variable: the informative label (e.g. -2 = “institution”) stays in the data but counts as missing (is.na()). A to_factor variable comes out as a haven_labelled_spss vector of label text instead of a factor with the missing reasons as levels (a factor can’t mark a level missing). labelled::to_factor() turns it into that factor; labelled::to_factor(user_na_to_na = TRUE) into one without them (#27).
  • With standardize, a missing-value code whose meaning differs between waves keeps its code for the meaning the documentation introduced first; a later meaning moves to the code another wave gives it, or else to a free code (-9, then -99, -98, …). For example, 272’s -4 is “short version” in wave C and “do not know” from D on, which now reads as -9 (#27).
  • Harmonized missing codes are labelled with what the waves say (e.g. “na, see MOVED”, “institution”), no longer with a label made up to cover several reasons (“not available, routing”, “response unavailable”) (#27).

Value labels

  • A variable whose answer labels differ between waves (e.g. 161’s remarks, 1 = "no" in C but 1 = "yes" in 2B) is now var_type “text”: with standardize it reads as a factor whose levels are every wave’s answers, the same at every wave, or as plain text with to_factor = FALSE. Its harmonized labels no longer join several waves’ labels (“no / yes”). Without standardize, every variable gets its own wave’s labels, as a factor with to_factor (#27).
  • Codes that share a label, such as z004 anation’s 19 and 23 (“Italian”), are now one factor level instead of “Italian [19]” and “Italian [23]” (#27).
  • A text variable’s code that its wave doesn’t label falls back to the harmonized label (e.g. 035 hart14 at wave B) (#27).
  • Categorical items typed numeric are now categorical: 035 incon9, incon10, cva02, cva02b, hart06, kneep5, kneep9; 161 mgriplp3/4, mgriprp3/4, mweightp7, rm161; 033 health3, health4; 045 erh, sych; 154 msmokecigpnw; 158 mpeakfc; 184 mmilka50y, mmilkb25y; 435 xcara07, xcara08, xcva02, xdiabe12, xhart06, xhart11. z004 aedu stays numeric: it is years of education, and its labels name each number of years’ level (#27).
  • The label database has a new table, value_labels_crosswalk, listing how a wave’s codes read under standardize.

CleanLASA 1.0.0

First stable release.

New features

  • transform_lasa_data() reshapes LASA data between wide format (one row per respondent, as in Z files) and long format (one row per respondent per wave). Long format has a Wave column and a Time column that counts waves from each respondent’s own cohort baseline (B, 2B, 3B, MB or 4B). Merged and stacked files work too.
  • read_lasa_sav(format_as_long = TRUE) returns a file in long format straight away.
  • Wide output can name columns by wave (prefix = "Wave") or by time since baseline (prefix = "Time"). Time-prefixed data carries a cohort column that merges with LASAZ002.sav’s.
  • Cross-wave Z files such as LASAZOA1.sav are now labelled and converted to factors.

Missing values

  • The new keep_user_na argument decides what happens to missing-value codes, and it does the same thing for every variable type. With FALSE (the default), every missing code becomes NA. With TRUE, every missing code is kept, as label text or as a declared-missing haven_labelled_spss value. user_na is deprecated: a supplied value is used as keep_user_na, with a warning.
  • Discrete negative codes are always treated as missing, even when the label sounds substantive (e.g. “never had job” or “valid score”). Variables whose genuine values can be negative (e.g. dB thresholds) keep those values. The label database marks them with can_be_negative.

Label database

  • Fixed many gaps and errors in the bundled label database, including the ones reported in #18.
  • “na, see …” routing labels now name only the referenced variable.
  • Codes that have no wording are named after their number. Listed values of numeric variables that have no wording are dropped.
  • The bundled database is now found even without library(CleanLASA).

Package

  • Now requires R 4.0.0 or later.
  • The introduction vignette is now built as a proper package vignette.
